title: Attention from scratch
objectives: Write causal multi-head attention in NumPy inside twenty minutes, the pace of the drill after it, with the shapes checked.

screens.title: Shapes first
screens.prose: This lesson takes about fifteen minutes; the drill after it has a pace of twenty minutes. You built masked multi-head attention in `sequence` level 3. In an interview, fix the shapes before any code: $\mathbf{x}$ is $T \times d$ with $T = 5$ tokens and $d = 8$, one head.
screens.question: Fill in the shapes, rows by columns.

hints.text: $\mathbf{Q}$ has a row per token and a column per feature.
Scores compare every query with every key: token by token.
Weights times $\mathbf{V}$ give a $d$-wide row per token again.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Follow the shapes through each product.

byKey.d-cols: Scores are query against key, so they are $T \times T$, not $T \times d$.
byKey.T-cols: The output mixes value rows, which are $d$ wide.

explain.text: Scores are $T \times T$: one row per query, one column per key. The output is $T \times d$ like the input, which is why blocks stack.

screens.title: The order to write it
screens.prose: Two tokens, $d = 2$, one head: $\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{I}$, $\mathbf{W}_q = \mathbf{W}_v = \mathbf{W}_o = \mathbf{I}$, $\mathbf{W}_k = [[1, 1], [0, 2]]$. Step through the middle of the computation.

frames.caption: masked: a query never sees a later key

screens.question: Order the lines as you would write them. Leave out the line that does not belong.

lines.text: Set scores above the diagonal to $-\infty$.
Weights times $\mathbf{V}$, then merge the heads.
Softmax each row, then zero the entries above the diagonal.
lines.why: Zeroing after the softmax leaves rows that no longer sum to 1, and the future already shaped the normaliser.

feedback.correct: Project, split, score and scale, mask, softmax, mix and merge, project.
feedback.generic: Not quite. The mask must come before the softmax.

byKey.ax: Masking after the softmax lets future tokens into the normaliser.

explain.text: Say each line as you write it, with its shape. The mask goes in before the softmax, so a masked score becomes an exact 0 weight.

screens.title: One row by hand
screens.prose: The second query sees both keys, with scaled scores $1/\sqrt{2}$ and $2/\sqrt{2}$.
screens.question: What weight does the second query give the first token? Give 4 decimal places.

hints.text: Softmax of two numbers $a < b$ gives $1/(1 + e^{b - a})$ to the smaller.
Here $b - a = 1/\sqrt{2}$.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Apply the softmax to the second row.

byKey.swapped: That is the weight on the second token, the larger score.
byKey.uniform: The two scores differ, so the weights do too.

explain.text: The row softmax gives $(0.3302, 0.6698)$. With $\mathbf{W}_v = \mathbf{W}_o = \mathbf{I}$ the output rows equal the weight rows.

screens.title: Which entries to mask
screens.prose: Four tokens. Row $i$ is query $i$, column $j$ is key $j$. A token may look at itself and earlier tokens.
screens.question: Tap every score that must be set to $-\infty$.

hints.text: Query 1 may see key 1 only.
Mask where the key comes after the query: $j > i$.
That is the upper triangle, without the diagonal.

feedback.correct: The strict upper triangle: six entries.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Mask keys later than the query.

byKey.lower: You masked the past. A token must not see the future: keys with $j > i$.
byKey.diag: A token may attend to itself; leave the diagonal.

explain.text: Six of the sixteen scores are masked, $j > i$. The diagonal stays, so every row has at least one key and no row is fully masked.

screens.title: Several heads
screens.prose: With $h$ heads, each head works on $d_h = d/h$ columns, and its scores are divided by $\sqrt{d_h}$. Take $d = 64$ and 8 heads.
screens.question: By what number is each head's score divided? Give 4 decimal places.

hints.text: Each head has $64/8$ columns.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Use the head's width, $d/h$.

byKey.full-d: That is $\sqrt{64}$, the full width. Each head's dot product runs over $d_h = 8$ columns.

explain.text: Each head's dot product sums $d_h = 8$ terms, so its sd is $\sqrt{8} = 2.8284$. Dividing by $\sqrt{64}$ would shrink the scores too far and flatten the weights.

screens.title: Mask after the softmax?
screens.prose: A candidate softmaxes the full score row, then multiplies by a 0/1 mask to drop future keys.
screens.question: What goes wrong?

options.text: Rows stop summing to 1; the future sets the normaliser.
Nothing: the masked weights are 0 either way.
options.why: They are 0, but the kept weights were divided by a sum that included the future.

options.text: Only speed: it does an extra multiplication.
options.why: The result itself is wrong: the first row would keep about $0.67$, not 1.

options.text: It gives nan for the first row.
options.why: There is no $-\infty$ here, so nothing becomes nan.

hints.text: Compute the first row both ways.
Softmax first: $(0.67, 0.33)$; masking leaves $(0.67, 0)$.
Masking first gives $(1, 0)$.

feedback.correct: The future leaks through the normaliser.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Compare the first row masked before and after.

byKey.fine: The kept weight is $0.67$ instead of 1: the future key took a third of the mass.

explain.text: Softmax first gives the first row $(0.6698, 0.3302)$, and the mask leaves $(0.6698, 0)$. The row no longer sums to 1, and its size depends on a key the token must not see. Zeroing after the softmax and renormalising would also work, but masking first is the norm: it avoids exponentiating scores that are thrown away.

screens.title: One token
screens.prose: Edge case: $T = 1$. The single query sees only its own key.
screens.question: What is its attention weight, whatever the score?

hints.text: A softmax over one entry.
$e^s / e^s$.
It is 1.

feedback.correct: Always 1: the output is the token's own value, projected.
feedback.generic: Not quite. A softmax over one entry is always the same.

byKey.zero: Zero would mean the token attends to nothing. Softmax weights sum to 1, so the single key takes all of it.

explain.text: A softmax over one entry is $e^s/e^s = 1$. Say it in the interview: with $T = 1$ the code must still run, and the output is $\mathbf{v}\mathbf{W}_o$.

screens.title: The cost, aloud
screens.prose: The scores take $T^2 d$ multiply-adds and the weighted sum the same. So attention costs $$O(T^2 d)$$ time, and $O(T^2)$ memory per head for the weights.
screens.question: Doubling the context length $T$ multiplies the score cost by what?

feedback.generic: Not quite. The cost grows with $T^2$.

byKey.linear: Linear in $T$ would be 2; the scores grow with $T^2$.

explain.text: Every query meets every key, so the work grows with $T^2$: twice the context, 4 times the cost. That is the number behind long-context research.

screens.title: Next: a KV cache
screens.prose: A lab interviewer says: "Your model now generates one token at a time. Make step $t$ cheap."
screens.question: What changes at step $t$?

options.text: Project only the new token; append its key and value to a cache and attend over all $t$.

options.why: That repeats work done on earlier steps. Past keys and values do not change.

options.text: Drop the mask, since there is no future during generation.
options.why: Without future tokens the mask has nothing to hide, but that is not what saves time.

options.text: Attend to the last token only.
options.why: That changes the model. The new query still attends over every earlier key.

hints.text: Which keys and values change when one token is added?
None of the earlier ones.
Store them and compute only the new row: $O(t\,d)$ a step.

feedback.correct: Cache past keys and values; one new query row per step.
feedback.generic: Not quite. Ask what is unchanged from the last step.

byKey.all: Earlier keys and values are fixed; recomputing them is the waste.

explain.text: With a cache, step $t$ needs one query, one new key and value, and a row of $t$ scores. The cost per step is $O(t\,d)$ instead of $O(t^2 d)$.

Splits the columns by striding, so head 0 takes every other column.
Forgets the transpose and returns (T, heads, d_h).

hints.text: Reshape to $(T, h, d_h)$ first: that cuts each row into consecutive blocks.
Then move the head axis to the front.
`x.reshape(T, h, d // h).transpose(1, 0, 2)`.

feedback.correct: Each head holds a consecutive block of columns for every token.
feedback.generic: Not yet. Cut each row into blocks, then move the head axis first.

byKey.test-1: The shape is off. Move the head axis to the front: `(h, T, d_h)`.
byKey.test-2: Head 0 holds the wrong numbers. Reshape to `(T, h, d_h)` before the transpose; a straight reshape or a stride mixes tokens or columns.

explain.text: Reshape keeps memory order, so `(T, h, d_h)` cuts each token's row into consecutive blocks. The transpose only reorders axes; merging heads later is the reverse.

screens.title: The mask
screens.prose: Write `mi_causal_mask(T)`: a $T \times T$ array to add to the scores, 0 where key $j \le$ query $i$ and $-\infty$ where $j > i$.
screens.question: Complete the function.

widget.starter:
import numpy as np


def mi_causal_mask(T):
    # (T, T): 0 where key j <= query i, -inf where j > i; add it to the scores
    ...
widget.solution:
import numpy as np


def mi_causal_mask(T):
    m = np.zeros((T, T))
    m[np.triu_indices(T, k=1)] = -np.inf
    return m
widget.how: Submit runs 5 hidden tests: the full 3 by 3 mask, $T = 1$, the count of masked entries for $T = 6$, the diagonal for $T = 5$, and the lower triangle for $T = 4$. Values are compared exactly.

mutants.symptom: Writes 1 instead of minus infinity, a multiplicative mask added to the scores.

hints.text: Start from zeros.
`np.triu_indices(T, k=1)` gives the strict upper triangle.
Set those entries to `-np.inf`.

feedback.correct: The strict upper triangle is $-\infty$, the rest 0.
feedback.generic: Not yet. Mask keys later than the query, and nothing else.

byKey.test-1: The 3 by 3 mask is off. Put $-\infty$ strictly above the diagonal ($j > i$), keep the diagonal at 0, and add it to the scores.

explain.text: Added to the scores, $-\infty$ becomes $e^{-\infty} = 0$ in the softmax. The diagonal stays 0, so no row is ever fully masked.

screens.title: The follow-up
screens.prose: The interviewer goes on: "Make it batched." Then sit the drill `#drill/mi-causal-attention` (pace 20 minutes): your attention, whole, with heads and the mask.
screens.question: What do the scores look like for a batch of $B$ sequences?

options.text: Shape $(B, h, T, T)$, with one $(T, T)$ mask broadcast over both.
A Python loop over the batch, calling the unbatched code each time.
options.why: It works, but the interviewer asked you to vectorise.

options.text: Shape $(BT, BT)$, stacking all sequences into one.
options.why: That lets tokens of one sequence attend to another; it needs a block mask and does $B$ times the work.

hints.text: Add a batch axis in front of every array.
Each sequence and head gets its own $T \times T$ scores.
One mask of shape $(T, T)$ broadcasts over the first two axes.

feedback.generic: Not quite. Keep sequences separate and vectorise.

byKey.flat: One big matrix lets sequences see each other.

explain.text: Batching adds a leading axis: `np.einsum('bhtd,bhsd->bhts', Q, K)` gives $(B, h, T, T)$ and the mask broadcasts. Say the memory cost, $B h T^2$ numbers for the weights.

ideas: Fix the shapes aloud first: $\mathbf{x}$ is $T \times d$, scores are $T \times T$ per head, the output is $T \times d$.
Write it in order: project, split heads, score over $\sqrt{d_h}$, mask, softmax, mix, merge, project.
Mask before the softmax with $-\infty$; masking after it lets the future set the normaliser. Cost: $O(T^2 d)$.
summary.trap: Masking after the softmax leaves rows that do not sum to 1 and lets later tokens shape them.

quiz.prose: One head, causal. Query 3 has scaled scores $(0, 0, \ln 2)$ against keys 1 to 3.
quiz.question: What weight does it give key 3?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Exponentiate and normalise the row.

byKey.uniform: The third score is larger, so its weight is too.
byKey.raw: That is the score, not the weight.

explain.text: The exponentials are $1, 1, 2$, which sum to 4, so key 3 gets $2/4 = 0.5$.

quiz.question: A causal mask for $T = 10$: how many entries are $-\infty$?

feedback.generic: Not quite. Count the strict upper triangle.

byKey.all: Only keys after the query are masked.

explain.text: The strict upper triangle of a $10 \times 10$ matrix holds $10 \times 9/2 = 45$ entries.

quiz.question: A model has $d = 512$ and 8 heads. By what is each head's score divided?

byKey.dh: That is $d_h$ itself; take its root.

explain.text: Each head has $d_h = 64$ columns, so its scores are divided by $\sqrt{64} = 8$.
